import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders. # Placeholders are surrounded by double curly braces for clarity. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{{post_heading}}

Posted by: {{author_id}}

{{content}}
{{labels}}
""" def render_blog_post(author_id: str, post_heading: str, content: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Render a secure, XSS‑protected HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- author_id : str Identifier of the post's creator. post_heading : str Heading/title of the post. content : str Main body of the post. May contain user‑supplied markup that must be escaped. labels : list[str] Sequence of tags/labels to display. Each will be wrapped in a . Returns ------- str A fully escaped HTML string ready for rendering in a browser. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of the expected type. """ # Basic type checks (prevent accidental injection from non‑string types) if not isinstance(author_id, str): raise TypeError("author_id must be a string") if not isinstance(post_heading, str): raise TypeError("post_heading must be a string") if not isinstance(content, str): raise TypeError("content must be a string") if not (isinstance(labels, list) and all(isinstance(l, str) for l in labels)): raise TypeError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape all user‑supplied content to neutralize HTML/JS injection. esc_author_id = html.escape(author_id, quote=True) esc_post_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=True) esc_content = html.escape(content, quote=False) # preserve newlines # Render each label as a safe escaped_labels = [] for tag in labels: esc_tag = html.escape(tag, quote=True) escaped_labels.append(f'{esc_tag}') # Join labels with a space for readability labels_html = " ".join(escaped_labels) # Replace placeholders in the template rendered = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( author_id=esc_author_id, post_heading=esc_post_heading, content=esc_content, labels=labels_html ) return rendered.strip()
